title: Equivariant curve-pencil preparation over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a normal proper geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension $d\geq2$, and let a finite group $H$ act on $X$ and $k$ compatibly with the structure morphism. The action need not be faithful. There are normal proper geometrically integral finite-type $k$-schemes $X'$ and $Y$, with compatible $H$-actions, an $H$-equivariant H-projective surjective birational morphism $\pi:X'\to X$, and an $H$-equivariant H-projective dominant morphism $g:X'\to Y$. The scheme $Y$ is projective and geometrically integral over $k$ of dimension $d-1$, and the generic fibre of $g$ is a geometrically integral curve. Birational here means that $\pi$ is an isomorphism over a dense open of $X$ and identifies the function fields. No smoothness of this generic curve is asserted.

Field, integrality, properness, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, H-projectivity, finite morphisms, surjectivity and function fields use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and [def-sc-function-field]. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target.
